SK1120 A reflection call asks what is answers

typeof(T).IsInstanceOfType(x) and typeof(T).IsAssignableFrom(x.GetType()) both spell x is T as a Type load and a virtual call.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0
ReSharperCanSimplifyIsInstanceOfType (resharper_can_simplify_is_instance_of_type_highlighting)
SupersedesCanSimplifyIsAssignableFrom

Why

The is operator is one IL instruction, and more to the point it is the spelling every C# reader recognises and the one that composes with a pattern — x is T t binds the value that the reflection call would need a separate, unchecked cast for. ⚠ Nothing in the shipped toolchain reports either shape, measured rather than assumed: compiled at AnalysisMode=All, AnalysisLevel=latest-all and EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true, with the whole Style and CodeQuality categories raised to warning, both shapes produce no IDE* and no CA* diagnostic. ⚠ The instrument was verified in the same build rather than trusted: planted shapes produce IDE0059 and IDE0090, so the zero beside them is a zero from clean analysis and not from analysis that never ran — and at the default EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true alone, no IDE* rule appears at all, because they ship enabled and Hidden.

Example

Instead of:

if (typeof(Stream).IsInstanceOfType(source)) {
    Copy(source);
}

if (typeof(Stream).IsAssignableFrom(source.GetType())) {
    Copy(source);
}

Write:

if (source is Stream) {
    Copy(source);
}

if (source is Stream) {
    Copy(source);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ The two shapes are one concept and they are not equally safe, which is why the rule ships `fixIsSafe: false` although one half of it is exactly total. Fourteen shapes were compiled and run for IsInstanceOfType — null, a boxed value type, a non-null and a null int?, an interface, a covariant interface, array covariance, an array through IList<T>, an enum boxed as itself and as its underlying int, and a wrong type — and the reflection call and the operator agree on every one. IsAssignableFrom(x.GetType()) agrees on six of the same shapes and diverges on the seventh: x.GetType() throws NullReferenceException where x is T is false. A rule carries one safety answer and the pair takes the weaker one. ⚠ The nullable-value-type divergence this rule was expected to have does not exist, and the expectation is refuted. Type.IsAssignableFrom documents — and the probe confirms — a special case for a nullable value type and its underlying type: typeof(int?).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(int)) is true, and (object)someInt is int? is true as well, so the two agree. ⚠ Three types make `typeof(T)` compile and `x is T` not compile, all three confirmed against the compiler rather than assumed: a static class, a `ref struct`, and an unbound generic such as typeof(List<>). Each is a legal reflection call and an uncompilable pattern, and each is declined; void, a pointer, a function pointer and an error type are declined for the same reason. ⚠ `typeof(A).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(B))` is never reported, declined by construction rather than by a name list: the argument is required to be a GetType() call, and a question about two types with no value in it has no is spelling at all. ⚠ `SK2181`'s shape is handed over by the BCL rather than by a guard, and the guard written for it was removed as unreachable. System.Type declares its own public new Type GetType(), so t.GetType() on a Type receiver binds to System.Type.GetType() and never to object.GetType() — asked directly, the model answers System.Type.GetType() with containing type System.Type. Requiring the GetType() to be object's therefore already declines every expression SK2181 owns, and removing the explicit handover turned no fixture red because there was nothing left for it to do. ⚠ The operand must be a reference type. int n; n is object is CS0183, "the given expression is always of the provided type" — a warning the fix would introduce, which the fixture harness' re-binding test correctly treats as a broken fix. A value operand boxes into the reflection call and is a different, rarer shape; it is declined rather than reported without a usable edit. ⚠ CS8121: a target type that no conversion reaches from the operand's type is declined through ClassifyConversion, because the reflection call is legal there and always false while the pattern does not compile at all. ⚠ The operand must be a primary expression, because the rewrite moves it from an argument position, where every precedence is legal, to the left of a relational operator, where most are not — a ? b : c is T does not mean (a ? b : c) is T. ⚠ The replacement is parenthesised wherever the call was an operand of an expression: !typeof(T).IsInstanceOfType(x) becomes !(x is T), and without the parentheses it parses as (!x) is T and does not compile. ⚠ The type is re-spelled from the typeof operand's own source text rather than from the symbol, so the edit needs no using the file does not have and no qualification the file does not use. A comment or a preprocessor directive inside the replaced span withdraws the finding. Generated code is excluded.
